title: Indirect Questions: Could you tell me…?
grammarTitle: Indirect Questions — polite and formal ways to ask
grammarNote: Косвенные вопросы (indirect questions) — это вопросы, встроенные в другую, более вежливую структуру. Они звучат более тактично, чем прямые вопросы, особенно в формальных ситуациях (собеседования, незнакомые люди, официальные контексты). Ключевое правило: в косвенном вопросе слова НЕ инвертируются (подлежащее стоит перед глаголом, как в утвердительном предложении).

grammarTable.subject: Direct question
grammarTable.example: "Where IS the library?" / "What TIME does it start?" / "WHO are you?"

grammarTable.subject: Indirect question
grammarTable.example: "Could you tell me where the library IS?" / "Do you know what time IT STARTS?"

grammarTable.subject: Introducing phrase
grammarTable.example: "Could you tell me / Do you know / I'd like to know / I wonder..."

grammarTable.subject: Yes/No → whether/if
grammarTable.example: "Is there a café?" → "Do you know WHETHER/IF there is a café?"

grammarTable.subject: Wh- stays
grammarTable.example: "Where is it?" → "Do you know WHERE it is?" (wh-word stays at the beginning)

grammarTable.subject: No do/does/did
grammarTable.example: "What time DOES it start?" → "Do you know what time IT STARTS?" (drop does!)

grammarExtra.title: Step-by-step: How to form indirect questions

rows.form: Step 1: Start with a polite phrase
rows.example: "Could you tell me..." / "Do you know..." / "I wonder..." / "I'd like to know..."

rows.form: Step 3: Use NORMAL word order (no inversion)
rows.example: "...where the library IS." (NOT "where IS the library")
"...what time it STARTS." (NOT "what time DOES it start")

grammarExtra.title: Common introducing phrases — from most to least formal

rows.example: "Could you tell me...?" / "Would you be able to tell me...?"
"Can you tell me...?" / "Do you know...?" / "I'd like to know..."
"I wonder if you could tell me...?" / "I was wondering where..."
"Do you happen to know...?" / "Could you possibly tell me...?"
"Do you know WHETHER/IF the café is open?" (NOT "Do you know is the café open?")
"whether" is more formal. Both are correct. "Do you know if she arrived?" ✅
"...whether the café IS open." (not "...whether IS the café open?")
✗ "Do you know whether IS she coming?" → ✅ "Do you know whether SHE IS coming?"

grammarExtra.title: ❌ Most common mistakes with indirect questions

rows.form: ✗ "Could you tell me where IS the library?"
rows.example: ✅ "Could you tell me WHERE THE LIBRARY IS?" — no inversion!

rows.form: ✗ "Do you know what time does it start?"
rows.example: ✅ "Do you know WHAT TIME IT STARTS?" — drop "does"!

rows.form: ✗ "I'd like to know is she coming."
rows.example: ✅ "I'd like to know WHETHER SHE IS coming." — use whether for yes/no!

rows.form: ✗ "Could you tell me who are you?"
rows.example: ✅ "Could you tell me who you are?" — subject before verb!

grammarTip:
Косвенные вопросы — три золотых правила:
① Начни с вежливой фразы: "Could you tell me / Do you know / I'd like to know..."
② Слова НЕ инвертируются: "...where the library IS" (НЕ "where IS the library")
③ Убери do/does/did: "...what time it STARTS" (НЕ "does it start")

Для вопросов типа yes/no → используй WHETHER или IF:
"Do you know WHETHER she is coming?"

💡 Тест: если в прямом вопросе есть "is / are / was / were" — перенеси его ПОСЛЕ подлежащего:
"Where IS the café?" → "...where the café IS."

Если есть "do/does/did" — УБЕРИ его:
"What time DOES it start?" → "...what time it STARTS."

exercises.text: "Where is the library?" → "Could you tell me ___ ?"
exercises.hint: No inversion in indirect: subject + verb. "...where THE LIBRARY IS." ✅ (not "where IS the library")

exercises.text: "What time does the lecture start?" → "Do you know what time ___ ?"
exercises.hint: Drop "does", no inversion: "...what time IT STARTS." ✅

exercises.instruction: Convert the yes/no question to indirect.
exercises.text: "Is there a café near here?" → "Do you know ___ a café near here?"
exercises.hint: Yes/no direct → "whether/if" + normal order. "...WHETHER THERE IS a café." ✅

exercises.text: "Could you tell me where does the bus stop?" is correct.
exercises.hint: ✅ "Could you tell me WHERE THE BUS STOPS?" — drop "does" and use normal word order!
"Could you tell me WHO YOU ARE?" — no inversion. subject (you) + verb (are). ✅

exercises.text: "Has she applied?" → "Do you know ___ she has applied?"
exercises.hint: Yes/no question → whether or if. "Do you know WHETHER/IF she has applied?" ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the most formal introducing phrase.
exercises.text: "___ you could tell me the way to the dean's office?"
exercises.hint: "Could you tell me...?" is more formal than "Can you tell me...?" — use "Could" in formal/interview contexts. ✅

exercises.text: "What is the application deadline?" → Choose the correct indirect form.
opts: "Do you know what is the application deadline?"
"Do you know what the application deadline is?"
"Do you know what the application deadline are?"
"Do you know what application deadline is?"
exercises.correct: "Do you know what the application deadline is?"
exercises.hint: "Do you know WHAT THE APPLICATION DEADLINE IS?" — no inversion, subject before verb. ✅

exercises.text: "Where does the professor live?" → "I'd like to know where ___."
exercises.hint: Drop "does", normal order: "...where THE PROFESSOR LIVES." ✅

exercises.text: "Did she get the scholarship?" → "Do you know ___ she got the scholarship?"
exercises.hint: "Did she...?" is a yes/no question → use "whether" (or "if") in indirect: "...WHETHER she got the scholarship." ✅

exercises.text: "I'd like to know is she happy there." is a correct indirect question.
exercises.hint: ✅ "I'd like to know WHETHER SHE IS happy there." — yes/no → whether + normal word order!

exercises.text: "How many students are in the group?" → "Could you tell me how many students ___?"
exercises.hint: No inversion needed: "how many students ARE IN THE GROUP?" — "are" comes after the subject. ✅

questions.text: "Where is the office?" → Indirect: "Could you tell me ___?"
questions.hint: "...where THE OFFICE IS." — no inversion! Subject + verb. ✅

questions.text: "What time does the seminar start?" → "Do you know ___?"
opts: what time does the seminar start
questions.hint: Drop "does", no inversion: "...what time THE SEMINAR STARTS." ✅

questions.text: "Is the library open?" → "Do you know ___ the library is open?"
questions.hint: Yes/no question → "whether" or "if". "...WHETHER THE LIBRARY IS open." ✅

questions.text: "Do you know where is the professor?" is correct.
questions.hint: ✅ "Do you know WHERE THE PROFESSOR IS?" — no inversion in indirect questions!

questions.text: "Who is in charge?" → "Could you tell me ___?"
questions.hint: "...who IS IN CHARGE." — no change needed here; "who" is the subject, so it comes first. ✅

questions.text: "Did she pass?" → "Do you know ___ she passed?"
questions.hint: "Did she...?" is yes/no → use "if" or "whether". "...IF she passed." ✅

questions.text: "How do I get to the dean's office?" → "Could you tell me how ___?"
questions.hint: "...how I GET there." — no inversion, drop "do": subject (I) + verb (get). ✅

questions.text: "What does WKU stand for?" → "I'd like to know what WKU ___."
questions.hint: Drop "does", normal order: "...what WKU STANDS FOR." ✅

questions.text: Which is a correct indirect question?
opts: "Do you know where does she work?"
"Could you tell me where she works?"
"I'd like to know where works she."
"Can you tell me where she work?"
questions.correct: "Could you tell me where she works?"
questions.hint: "...where SHE WORKS." — no inversion, correct 3rd person verb. ✅

questions.text: "Are there any seats available?" → "Do you know ___?"
opts: whether there are any seats available
questions.correct: whether there are any seats available
questions.hint: "WHETHER THERE ARE any seats available." — yes/no + normal word order. ✅

questions.text: Which introducing phrase is most formal?
questions.hint: "Could you tell me...?" is the most politely formal. "Could" is more formal than "can". ✅

questions.text: "When does the term end?" → "Could you tell me when the term ___?"
questions.hint: Drop "does", normal order: "...when the term ENDS." (3rd person -s) ✅
"I wonder WHERE SHE LIVES." — no inversion, normal order. ✅

questions.text: "Whether" and "if" are both correct for yes/no indirect questions.
questions.hint: "whether" and "if" can both introduce yes/no indirect questions. "whether" is slightly more formal. ✅

questions.text: "Who does she work for?" → "Do you know who ___?"
questions.hint: "Do you know who SHE WORKS FOR?" — drop "does", normal order. ✅ (Note: "for" stays at the end)

questions.text: The main difference between direct and indirect questions is:
opts: The word order (no inversion in indirect) and the introducing phrase
questions.correct: The word order (no inversion in indirect) and the introducing phrase
questions.hint: Indirect questions: (1) polite introducing phrase + (2) no inversion of subject+verb.
